quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and be ready to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for hazards. Workers may be present.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of in a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross safely. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: A steady green light means:

options.text: You may go through if it is safe and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through if it is safe and clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection. Always check for other traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection before proceeding.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Go ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Pull to the right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at crosswalks. Wait until they have crossed before you go.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and drugs?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and focus, increases reaction time, and greatly reduces coordination.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. A cold shower, exercise, or coffee will not help. It takes about one hour per drink.

questions.question: If you are not the first person at an accident and help is not needed, you should:

options.text: Stop and look at the scene.
Keep driving and stay out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and stay out of the way.
questions.explanation: If you are first at an accident, call 911. If you are not trained to help, keep driving. This prevents you from blocking emergency vehicles and protects you from other distracted drivers.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrup and cold medicine with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can hurt your driving ability. These include prescription drugs like tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrup and cold medicine, allergy medicine, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when gates are up.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when gates are up.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings with warning signs or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Create a habit when you get in and out of your car. Before you start the car, buckle your safety belt and check that all passengers do the same.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
Only if the traffic light is green for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming up ahead.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and use the brakes lightly.
Press the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, lift your foot off the gas slowly. Wait until the car has slowed down a lot before you use the brakes.

questions.question: The correct order of traffic light colors from top to bottom is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns drivers that traffic signals are at the next intersection.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars that are already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When another car is passing you, you should:

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving at the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, let the other car pass safely. Do not speed up. Let the car merge back into your lane safely.

questions.question: In Tennessee, emergency crossovers on the interstate can only be used by:

options.text: Any driver who needs to turn around when no other cars are nearby.
Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.
questions.explanation: In Tennessee, it is against the law for any driver to make a U-turn on an interstate highway. Only emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews can use emergency crossovers.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you must stop until they are safely away from your car. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: If you try to squeeze your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb, you could crash. Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: When you encounter an aggressive driver, the safest thing to do is get out of their way. Never try to compete with other drivers. Always follow the rules of the road to avoid crashes.

questions.question: This sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing without a signal. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for any trains and be prepared to stop if you see or hear one. Never try to race ahead of a train.

questions.question: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights and a stop arm out, you must stop. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is put away. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas where your vision gets blurry when you are tired.
Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move. Check the rear corners of your vehicle where blind spots are located.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood can affect a driver's:
questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect how well you think and move. Any amount of alcohol can hurt your ability to drive safely. Driving under the influence, even with a low blood alcohol level, is a crime.

questions.question: A "No passing zone" sign tells you:

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot legally pass another vehicle in that area. You are usually in an area where you cannot see far enough ahead, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: This bicyclist is signaling:
questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals to show other drivers what they plan to do. A left arm held straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and make it harder to see.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass the vehicle slowly at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see. Stop and only move forward after all pedestrians have finished crossing.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic from the right may be merging onto your road. Be ready to make room for merging vehicles.
